chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Joe Steele on the train, and Joe Jordan's gambling winnings
summary: Hinton asks for more pianists, and Whaley adds Joe Steele and Joe Jordan, who won a fortune at Monte Carlo and built the Jordan Building in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now what about this -- we mentioned Claude Hopkins. Who else was around -- we mentioned Lucky Roberts. The piano players who were in New York -- we mentioned all the guys in Boston, and we talked about Jelly Roll Morton, when you ran into him at the Lafayette Theatre, and we talked about Lucky Roberts, which you made the $75, and we mentioned Claude Hopkins, when you met him. Now who else was
around here -- piano players -- can you think of anybody, Tom? That was around ...
Joe Steel, I think we mentioned him. We mentioned him in New York, but he was also from Boston, which is another -- Boston piano players.

At the Conservatory of Music in Boston, he was up there in the conservatory nine years, and I -- see, we used to ride on the train, because he used to work outside, he used to work in one of the clubs, see.
We were talking about Joe Steel now, riding the train, you say?

He used to ride the train the same place where I used to work, go, but he'd work at a different see, and he used to talk to me about music, see? And I didn't listen -- there was another piano player, Joe Jordan, and he was an elderly man, and he won a million dollars over there in France, and in between shows, he'd be playing, I don't know what he was playing, but he won a million dollars and came over here and broke the job in Chicago.
You got to be kidding -- a black guy?
I heard that name in Chicago -- he went to Chicago, didn't he?
Yeah, he got a building there named the Jordan Building.
He really won that money, huh?
Oh yeah. He went down to where was it -- Monte Carlo? He used to go down there and gamble.
Wait a second. So we're talking about this guy, Joe Jordan and you were saying he went down to Monte Carlo. Now he was a piano player, right?
